newsitem.title: USA: Arrow Intl gets FDA nod for device.
newsitem.headline: Arrow Intl gets FDA nod for device.

text.p: Arrow International Inc said Monday it has received approval from the U.S Food and Drug Administration to begin marketing a new percutaneous thrombectomy device (PTD).
The device is designed to mechanically break up blood clots that frequently prevent the free flow of blood in arm grafts of patients undergoing hemodialysis treatment.

Based on a $600 per unit selling price, and an estimated 150,000 hemodialysis patients in the U.S. who require one or more treatments annually, the company estimates the domestic market potential for this new device at about $90 million.

In other news, the company said it completed its previously-announced purchase of Pfizer Inc's Strato/Infusaid implantable infusion pump business on July 15. Arrow said it expects this transaction will add between $4 million and $5 million in annual revenues.
Arrow makes disposable catheters and related products for critical and cardiac care.
